speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such work includes planning for and designing complex structures and machinery, supervising their construction, as well as maintaining their safe operation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Professional Engineers Act provides for the registration of PEs, regulates their conduct, and licenses entities supplying professional engineering services in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Act regulates the four prescribed branches of engineering which are directly relevant to our built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are civil, mechanical, electrical and chemical engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Not only do these PEs design and oversee the construction of structures, systems, plants and facilities, but they are also responsible for conducting regular checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Act provides a basis to hold PEs legally accountable for the important work that they do.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Act was last amended in December 2005.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Globalisation has opened new overseas markets but also brought in new players.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Singapore has been making a big push to raise productivity and quality in the built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Construction Industry Transformation Map (ITM) which will be launched later this year will set out strategies to help our construction industry move up the value chain and capture growth opportunities in Singapore and abroad.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: PEs will play an instrumental role in this effort.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To address the changing needs of the industry, the Ministry of National Development (MND) and the PE Board (PEB) undertook a comprehensive review of the Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have proposed three sets of amendments to strengthen the profession so that our PEs can do their work well.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One, raising the standards and professionalism of PEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As part of the review, we also sought the views of industry associations, Government agencies, institutes of higher learning and PEs, and received support for the proposed amendments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Allow me to go through each of these categories.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The first set of amendments is intended to raise the standards and professionalism of PEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given the crucial role played by the PEB, several are designed to strengthen the Board's role as an advocate and regulator.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we are proposing to expand the PEB's scope of functions to allow the Board to undertake more activities to develop the PE profession.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, PEB is limited to promoting learning and education in connection with engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The amendment in clause 6(b) will expand that role to include more development and advocacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, PEB will now be able to work with the Institution of Engineers and other industry associations to support the Construction ITM and assist with its implementation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes championing initiatives to push for the adoption of digital engineering, as well as pooling resources and conducting courses on relevant skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help to strengthen the capabilities of the profession.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we want to give PEB the flexibility to appoint any person to its committees to assist the Board.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, committee members can only come from PEB or be a PE or allied professional.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This can limit the work of some committees.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The amendment in clause 7 will allow the Board to tap on a wider range of expertise, such as lawyers and accountants, where necessary and appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we want to provide the Board with a wider range of tools to carry out its regulatory role.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes greater flexibility to calibrate penalties according to the severity of infringements of the Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, PEB is faced with rather binary choices.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It can either impose a penalty of up to S$20,000, or it can revoke licences to practise.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is in line with those of other specialised professions, such as architects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, the Board will have the option of taking a lighter touch through censuring errant firms for minor infringements where monetary penalties or licence revocation is too severe.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Fourth, we are proposing to allow the Board to appoint investigators to conduct more in-depth investigations for serious offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, the Board relies on statements and evidence voluntarily provided by parties.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But sometimes, cooperation may not be forthcoming from parties concerned.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The amendment in clause 21 will allow investigators to apply for warrants from Magistrates to search premises for evidence.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There will be conditions and limitations imposed on the investigators to ensure that these powers are not abused.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is not explicitly stated in the current Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The second broad set of amendments is designed to help Singapore-registered PEs capture overseas opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Singapore-registered PEs seeking to practise in another country generally need to go through the qualification process in that country.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This could include having practical experience in that country.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But Mutual Recognition Arrangements (MRAs) can help streamline this process.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clauses 9 and 10 will help to facilitate and support the execution of such MRAs, including the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) MRA which was signed in 2005.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ASEAN countries have been working together to implement the MRA's terms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ACPEs can apply to the professional authorities of other ASEAN countries to practise in collaboration with their local PEs there without having to go through the full qualification process.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These amendments make it easier for Singapore-registered PEs to offer their services in other ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As with all agreements of this nature, the benefits will be reciprocal.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Foreign engineers registered in ASEAN states can also be authorised by the Board to supply professional engineering services in Singapore, provided they do so in collaboration with our Singapore PEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But ultimately, our PEs stand to benefit, as they gain easier access to larger markets in our region.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That said, we will monitor our PEs' internationalisation experience through the MRA and work to resolve any issues that may arise.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The last set of amendments is pro-enterprise changes that make existing requirements less onerous.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, companies can only provide professional engineering services that PEs in their direct employment are qualified to offer.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As most firms do not have PEs in every discipline as permanent staff, this may limit their scope to bid for more complex projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clause 15(c) will now allow firms to expand their capabilities by subcontracting specialised professional engineering works to qualified specialist PEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, a company licensed in civil engineering could engage a specialist PE in geotechnical engineering as a consultant, thus allowing the firm to provide end-to-end services for projects involving underground geotechnical building works.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These include works of a temporary nature, like site offices or workers' quarters.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, builders cannot undertake any professional engineering work, unless they are licensed by the Board to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But most builders are unable to meet the requirements to qualify for a licence from the Board.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result, they have to engage external engineering consultancies for their projects, which may incur additional costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This amendment will streamline work processes for some builders, while maintaining safety standards by limiting the scope to certain low-risk temporary works.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The amendments will also put PEB in a stronger position to support the industry in its development, and to uphold higher standards of professionalism.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through these efforts, we hope that PEs in Singapore will continue to thrive both in our domestic market and overseas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We are moving into an era where engineering is, once again, leading the charge, be it in driverless motor vehicles, smart homes or even environmental protection.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But every so often, we hear of the waste of talent when those who are trained in engineering choose to go into other sectors, like the financial industry or into the corporate world.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have spoken about the pay and career progression of engineers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Government has started to remedy that, which will hopefully have a knock-on effect on the private sector.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But we also need to improve the "image" of engineering.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I will highlight two ways we can do so.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As our Prime Minister pointed out, the trend among top scholarship holders has shifted to economics and liberal arts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government will recalibrate the compass and point more students to take up subjects that support its Smart Nation projects.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will send a message to all students that engineering is an attractive and interesting career.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Institution of Engineers Singapore and myself have been making calls publicly for more top students to be channelled into engineering.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But when we saw this year's President's Scholars, our hopes were dashed again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If I can recall, there was only one in 2015.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Whenever I bring up this question in Parliament, the answer has always been "they lump engineering and science together." I would like to say that engineering and science, they are "same-same" but different.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we really think that engineers are important, and the President's Scholarship being the most prestigious scholarship on this island, I look forward to seeing a change in the next round of scholarship awards.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We often read in the media about local medical discoveries and scientific breakthroughs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, we get excited about driverless vehicles but not much said about the persons working behind the project.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We talk about tech startups but the focus is often on the founder, not the engineers and coders.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is this because the research work carried out in the universities here is not getting the recognition, or is it because they are not courting the media to get exposure on their work?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Or is it because the subject is too dry or too technical that it is difficult to have interesting articles?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, we need a concerted effort to build up the image and correct any wrong perception of the engineering profession.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need to promote the profession as one that offers a career, with rewards that commensurate with responsibilities and opportunities to move up the ladder.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Smart Nation project should be an awakening to parents, students and others.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   I have talked about salaries and promotion opportunities for engineers before.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I would like to put my focus on the "face" issue of the engineering sector.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many students still feel that engineering is difficult to study, the work is hard and yet the salary is not high; worse still, it is not respected.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, many engineering graduates go into other industries to work.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many scholarship holders have studied engineering and made great contributions to our country.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have talked about this issue for so long, yet amongst this year's President's Scholars, none studies engineering.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that next year will be different.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There should be more media coverage on engineering, too.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, what we often see is the technology itself or the founder of the tech company, not the engineers who work behind the scenes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we can work on these two areas, I believe our students will develop a different perspective of engineering.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the Bill's amendments.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It cannot be more timely to review expanding the functions of the PEB and enhance the scope of professional services.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This will help to deepen expertise within the industry and bring about opportunities for more cross-disciplinary training.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I note several key improvements in this amendment and would highlight a few here.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With the increasing number of infrastructural projects and heightened awareness of workplace safety, provision of a new register of authorised persons who can work with the PEs will give rise to accountability and mitigate risks.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Such a register, for example, the Registered Foreign PEs, also provides recognition and becomes a springboard for our engineers with broader job opportunities in another jurisdiction like the developing ASEAN market.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This will be further facilitated under the existing ASEAN MRA on Engineering Services.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Indirectly, this enables the smaller companies to undertake more complex projects, scale up and be not only restricted to projects where they have the relevant inhouse PE expertise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Over time, when the companies are willing to invest in cross-training their staff, these workers can enhance their skills through on-the-job training as they work alongside other experts.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Thirdly, the role of advocacy that PEB needs to promote.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Nothing beats having a known professional community to advocate for the profession, as it goes beyond the role of the registrar, regulating quality and the conduct of engineers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, such advocacy must be shaped with the objectives of lending support to our engineers in the trade over time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: PEB should be cognisant that such advocacy is not simply one with a focus on social presence but, more importantly, to develop the education front, continuous learning within the trade and building networks.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is heartening to know that PEB organises events for accreditation of partners and recognition of exemplary engineers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Through this, I hope PEB can put more emphasis in working with the education and industry sectors to see how best to maintain cohorts of engineers and assist agencies like the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Workforce Singapore (WSG) to strengthen partnerships with employers who are willing to offer internships and job placements for our aspiring engineers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It would be of PEB's keen interest to creatively find avenues for engineers to have cross-discipline training throughout their career and take on challenges in new areas or advancement overseas.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Thus, PEB must build the global and local networks to support the profession in scaling up over time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: On this positive note, I have some questions and suggestions to raise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is good that PEB is benchmarking the penalty against other industries.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Two, contractors can be exempted from applying for a licence to supply PE services if the PEs are providing services for the contractors' own projects.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How can checks and balances be put in place to ensure endorsements and regulations are complied with?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This change would help those PEs under such circumstances to begin practising sooner lest their skills become irrelevant after being detached from the industry during the stand-down period.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: On the other hand, discipline and upholding standards of a PE is critical.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I suggest for PEB to create a clear listing of rules for those violations which fall under no disciplinary actions required and show a differentiated list by gravity of offence that warrants deregistration of PEs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With this, Mr Speaker, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The PEB was set up to safeguard life, property and the welfare of the public by setting and maintaining high standards for registering PEs, and by regulating and advancing the practice of professional engineering.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: For PEB to take on the role of development of professional engineering is a natural progression as it has the resources and Government support that are required and the neutrality to allow the different engineering branches and professional engineering associations a platform to help brand and push forward the engineering profession such that customers and engineers alike recognise the value of a registered PE.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Continual upgrade of technical skills and project management skills and safety awareness education should be developed to help prevent engineering tragedies that lead to severe loss of lives.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: One, that determines "Professional Engineering Work" and why is it that only certain branches prescribed under section 10(A) are required to register?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Should there also be a qualification in terms of stipulated years of work experience and review of projects the engineer had managed or undertaken before allowing engineers to be certified?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This, indeed, will help protect the rights of PEs and prosecute the relevant parties that may be responsible.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: PEB should also work closely with other stakeholders, especially buyer of services, to ensure the PEs are subject to fair treatment and remunerations without being subject to undue commercial pressures, unfair and untenable contractual terms.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, there should be a watchdog to monitor industry practices on the above.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Much has been reported about the manpower crunch in the engineering sector due to the decreased attractiveness of the profession to young people.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The expanded role of PEB will help to further advance industry development and broaden its appeal as a profession to address the skills gap that currently exists.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We all know that engineers are important and it has also been reported that close to half of the economy relies on inputs from engineers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the question is, why not do this for all branches of engineering since this is the PEB?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why exclude other engineering branches, such as aerospace, marine and transportation?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Who then will help to regulate these branches of engineering?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that this is under the existing ASEAN MRA on Engineering Services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yew Hang, a Singaporean engineer, commented on Facebook and asked how we will ensure that PEs from different countries are of consistent quality and that they are familiar with local regulatory requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, will there be a case of 10 Registered Foreign PEs working with just one Registered PE?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yew Hang further raised, and I quote, "How do we ensure that companies and businesses do not overly favour foreign PEs over local PEs, creating too much competition and driving wages down?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will this lead to an erosion of our local engineering core, especially when we are already lacking in engineering talents and engineering is not seen as an attractive career for many youths today?" I would be grateful if the Minister can provide clarifications about this and help assure the engineers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We rely on engineers to design, operate, maintain and support the running of our economy in sectors ranging from manufacturing to finance and transportation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, developing a pool of talent in software engineering is an essential part of our push to become a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill is a welcomed step in revitalising engineering in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to this legislative amendment, I urge the Government to continue its efforts to strengthen the engineering core, such as through initiatives to deepen our public sector engineering capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Thanaletchimi asked about the scope of the PE Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In particular, why the Bill covers only the four prescribed branches of engineering, and how other branches of engineering will be regulated and supported.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng cited, as examples, aerospace, marine and transport.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The regulatory agencies overseeing safety of engineering works on aircraft, marine projects and land transportation rely on specific legislation as well as industry codes to enforce quality and safety requirements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, on top of that, it is open to some regulators to decide to specify in their legislation that certain works need to be undertaken or certified by PEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In such situations, PEB will come in and prescribe these as branches of professional engineering.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Board then becomes an important secondary lever for regulation of PEs doing this work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this is an evolving and continuing conversation between PEB and various sectoral regulators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One key consideration amongst many is whether sectoral regulators assess that it is necessary to add a further layer of regulation on PE involvement in order to secure certain levels of safety and quality standards in the work, over and beyond what they have managed to achieve under their primary regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If so, PEB will work with them to prescribe new branches of professional engineering.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked about experience requirements for PEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: PE candidates are already required to meet relevant experience requirements prior to key milestones of the qualification process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Details of such requirements, such as the duration and scope of work experience, will be further prescribed in the Act's subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about PEB's processes for issuing penalties to PEs and professional engineering practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She suggested that the Board create a list of violations to make clear which warranted deregistration.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To some extent, sections 17B and 26A of the Act already set out some of the situations under which a PE can be removed from the register and when a professional engineering practice may have its licence revoked.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For minor infringements, PEB may choose to issue a letter of censure to errant firms or errant PEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It would be hard to be more prescriptive beyond that, as the exact course of action will depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: PEB has to calibrate the penalty according to the severity of wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But sometimes, complex cases may need to be investigated by PEB or Disciplinary Committees appointed by PEB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Chan also asked about checks and balances for contractors who employ PEs to carry out professional engineering works on their own projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This amendment should not compromise safety or professional standards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, PEs undertaking these works will still need to fulfil the full requirements, including the scope of work prescribed under the relevant legislation, such as the Building Control Act.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, PEs employed by contractors will continue to be held accountable by the PE Code of Conduct, which requires them to carry out their duties in a professional and independent manner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And third, the PEs that contractors employ can only carry out professional engineering works on specified low-risk temporary works, such as site offices and temporary living quarters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan also asked if the public could seek advice and recourse through the Board in the event of contractual disputes with PEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Board is a professional body and does not provide dispute resolution services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Contractual disputes should be resolved through other avenues, like mediation or litigation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, if disputes arise because of a PE's alleged professional misconduct, members of the public can still file a complaint against the PE with the Board.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the processes and criteria for authorising Registered Foreign PEs (RFPEs) through the ASEAN MRA on Engineering Services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To start, a person seeking to become an RFPE in Singapore must first be admitted in his own country as an ASEAN Chartered PE (ACPE).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To do so, he has to meet the criteria set out in the ASEAN MRA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Basically, this means holding a recognised engineering degree, keeping up with Continuing Professional Development, being equipped with relevant experience in engineering practice, and being recognised as the equivalent of a PE in his own country.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Taken together, these criteria help to uphold the standards of ACPEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, an ACPE must submit an application to the Board before he can become an RFPE in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ACPEs and RFPEs are bound by both Singapore and international codes of professional conduct, as well as Singapore laws and regulations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means that any RFPE working in Singapore will be held accountable, both by our regulatory bodies and by the Singapore legal system.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether there will be restrictions on the number of RFPEs who can collaborate with each locally-registered PE, and whether there are measures to mitigate unhealthy foreign competition that could depress wages and weaken our local core.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the first point, PEB requires an RFPE to collaborate with one designated local PE.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is to ensure that the quality of supervision by the Singapore PE is not diminished.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as I mentioned earlier, the scheme is still in its early days, and the number of RFPEs in Singapore is still very small.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: PEB is monitoring the situation and will adjust the conditions in future if necessary.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the second point, RFPEs cannot undertake professional engineering work independently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They cannot sign off on submissions to regulatory agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, they will not be able to replace PEB-registered PEs as custodians of the safety of our engineering works.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Currently, the Singaporean Core of our PE profession is strong.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But separately and more importantly, we will continue to work with the industry to strengthen the capabilities and skills of our engineering core.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee spoke of the need to develop our engineering profession and improve its image.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Engineering is a core capability that we must build on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As she noted, giving scholarships has been an important means of attracting talent into engineering-related fields.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the prestigious Public Service Commission Engineering Scholarship was introduced last year to strengthen our pipeline for apex leadership positions in the engineering clusters within the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Various Ministries and Statutory Boards, such as MND, the Ministry of Defence, JTC, the Public Utilities Board, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, the Defence Science and Technology Agency and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), amongst others, also give out engineering scholarships in many different branches.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To grow engineering capabilities in the private sector, agencies, such as BCA and the IMDA, have been working with industry partners to award scholarships in various branches of engineering.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, BCA offers the BCA-Industry Built-Environment Scholarships and Sponsorships in collaboration with industry firms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These scholarships aim to encourage high calibre students to pursue an engineering career in the built environment sector in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So far, more than 200 industry firms have participated in this programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also continue to look into new ways to develop the profession.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We agree that media publicity can help shape perception, correct misimpressions and promote engineering as a good career choice.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in 2016, the Government launched a rebranding campaign to revitalise the profession's image and highlight its important contributions to society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, in fact, the new realm of digital engineering and the introduction of Design for Manufacturing and Assembly, and Virtual Design and Construction involving technology and virtual reality, have begun to make the built environment sector and the engineering profession a lot more attractive, especially to young people for whom technology is like fish in water.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also increased salaries for public sector engineers to ensure that these jobs remain attractive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These efforts aim to raise the standards of public sector engineers and set the benchmark for the wider profession.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For engineers in the Built Environment sector, the Construction ITM that will be launched later this year will include strategies to develop and strengthen the profession.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But one idea that has been floated is to introduce a capstone programme for graduating students to bring them up to speed on industry best practices and prepare them for work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also set up a task force comprising representatives from the Government, industry and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to incorporate relevant skills into the engineering curricula of our tertiary education.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The task force is expected to deliver their recommendations early next year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I agree with Er Dr Lee on the importance of upskilling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is already a comprehensive suite of SkillsFuture programmes designed to help Singaporeans develop skills and competencies for future growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All of these schemes cover specialised courses in various fields of engineering.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SkillsFuture Earn and Learn programme aims to help fresh graduates from polytechnics and the Institutes of Technical Education augment their academic training with practical industry experience to support their transition into the workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Candidates undergo a 12- to 18-month structured training programme in a job related to their field of study.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The training programme includes guided learning, on-the-job training and work-based projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SkillsFuture Study Award is targeted at early- to mid-career Singaporeans looking to enhance their skills in future growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Eligible courses in the Built Environment sector include those from the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University and BCA Academy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to work with the Future Economy Council, IHLs and industry associations to review and update the list of qualifying courses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, there are many resources that our engineers can tap on to upskill and deepen their expertise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I encourage interested parties to find out more about the relevant schemes and qualifying courses on the SkillsFuture website before applying for the ones that are most suitable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With that, Mr Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.
